title: Titanium Bone Screw
alloyReason: ASTM F136 Ti-6Al-4V ELI is specified for this trauma fixation implant-grade component where controlled interstitials deliver high fatigue strength (>600 MPa @10^7 cyc) and corrosion resistance for permanent implantable devices. This rationale is driven by cortical/cancellous locking compression bone screw and service environment demands.
process: CNC swiss turning for trauma fixation geometry
Ultrasonic clean Class 10k with 0.5mm corner radius
surfaceTreatment: Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for corticalcancellous locking compression application
commonFailures: Fe contamination from machining - requires acid passivation 20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C per ASTM F86 — critical for corticalcancellous locking compression performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Bone Screw suitable for Cortical/cancellous locking compression bone screw?
faq.a: Titanium Bone Screw uses Ti-6Al-4V ELI because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address trauma fixation operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Bone Screw?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Bone Screw is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for corticalcancellous locking compression requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Bone Screw require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. corticalcancellous locking compression components require Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for corticalcancellous locking compression application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Bone Screw shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Bone Screw includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet corticalcancellous locking compression specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Bone screw / Cortical screw trauma fixation components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
